Docs: the VPN host. The Linux README (the second binary, how it fits together, dev keeping the VPN service in its own process), the source layout's heads and the signed set; CHANGELOG.Packages: a desktop head needs its VPN host head, or every connect fails.

Packaging: the VPN host beside the app. The Windows publish checks it among the signed executables; the Linux installer and launcher make it executable, as a package made on Windows carries no exec bit. Both scripts read VhAppVpnHostName as they read the command's name: the installer takes it as vpnHostNameParam, the launcher from publish.json's VpnHostFile, which a server's leaves empty.

Desktop: the VPN service runs in an executable of its own, the VPN host, as on the phones and in the Store: the app's service starts it at each connect, and it ends with its session. A head per product and OS - Client's and Connect's Windows.VpnHost and Linux.VpnHost - whose Main is one call into the device's project, WindowsVpnHost.Run or LinuxVpnHost.Run, with Core alone. Its name is VhAppVpnHostName, $(VhAppPackageTitle)VpnHost unless the app names its own, which the desktop heads carry as metadata and reference, so a build puts both executables in one folder over one runtime. It writes the service's system sinks from its first line (the Event Log under the service's name, the journal) and its own vpn.log, and the service logs one that ended without its session, with its exit code. One runs at a time: a start ends one still running. Windows: a kill-on-close job ends it with the service's process, the updater left outside; the kill switch lets out the service's SID - the service and what it starts - in place of the service's executable, and service install sets the SID type to unrestricted, which puts that SID in their tokens. Linux: the unit's stop sends it SIGTERM, on which it closes its session, 8 s at most. dev keeps the VPN service in its own process, for one debugger run. Accepted on Windows 11, Ubuntu 26.04 and Debian 13: connects, the kill switch and lockdown, a kill by hand, the service's restart, crash, stop and update, another app's takeover.
